facts.fact: planModel.ts defines one normalized plan model; planParsers/*.ts parse each dialect's differing EXPLAIN output into it (P18 v1.1, D16).
Plan model `metrics` projects every other dialect-reported field as label/value pairs; dialect fields survive parsing verbatim, nothing server said discarded.
Plan model `raw` keeps exact server EXPLAIN text; parse never claimed authoritative because SQLite's EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN format may change between releases (F14).
SQLite has no single EXPLAIN blob, so its parser reconstructs `raw` as one line per row in id/parent/notused/detail shape.
CostUnit is 'postgres-planner' | 'mysql-cost' | 'mariadb-cost' | 'none': unit of dialect's native cost figure, never compared across dialects.
MariaDB's and MySQL's identically-named `cost` disagree by three orders of magnitude for comparable scan, so costs not compared across dialects (F17).
CostUnit 'none' covers SQLite and ClickHouse, which report no cost.
Plan node's label is its own kind plus relation it touches when dialect names one, e.g. "Seq Scan on t", "SCAN t", "ReadFromMergeTree default.t".
Plan node's `detail` holds dialect's own condition/filter text verbatim: Postgres Filter, MySQL/MariaDB attached_condition, ClickHouse Indexes[].Condition, or SQLite's detail string.
estimatedRowsRead (D14) is max estimated-rows-read over plan's scan-type nodes for postgres/mysql/mariadb, or ClickHouse's EXPLAIN ESTIMATE sum.
estimatedRowsRead absent on sqlite, which reports no estimate.
Plan-level `issues` is roll-up of every node's issues, deduplicated by code; panel lists it above the tree.
overThreshold true only when estimatedRowsRead exists and meets or exceeds configured threshold.
D19's auto-explain warning trigger is `overThreshold || issues.some(i => i.severity === 'warn')`, because structural issue such as full scan can fire with no row estimate (sqlite).
ScanEstimate holds every scan/read-type PlanNode a dialect parser found, with row estimate, threaded through planIssues.ts.
D15 wide-scan issue and plan-level estimatedRowsRead/overThreshold derive from same ScanEstimate node set, never two passes that could disagree.
